title: The writing system and the ‘tooth’ family
text: Start with five letters In this first unit you will learn to recognise ا، ب، ت، ث، ن, distinguish their dots and build your first words. You do not need to memorise everything at once: read a step, try the exercises and revisit anything you find difficult. ⁧ا   ب   ت   ث   ن⁩ You are studying Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), the variety used in formal writing, documents and news broadcasts. Dialects will be covered separately. How to use this lesson In “Learn” you will find explanations and examples. In “Practice” you answer one question at a time and receive feedback. You can retry freely: the course keeps your answers and the points you need to review. Start with “First steps”: ten guided questions. Then move on to the course exercises. There are no lives to lose and no time limit. Lesson overview In this lesson learn how Arabic scripture works and read and write the first five letters ( ⁧ا ب ت ث ن⁩ ) with all the short vowels: in the end you read and write ten true words. Item Details Code L0-01 Level 0 · literacy (pre-A1 on the CEFR scale) Prerequisites None Estimated time 5–7 hours · one week at a standard pace Materials This unit, calligraphy notebook (Part V), Level Anki deck 0, pencil, striped notebook, phone to register Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. explain how Arabic writing works: direction, consonants and vowels, connection, forms of letters; 2. recognize, pronounce and write ⁧ا ب ت ث ن⁩ in all their forms; 3. read and write syllables with fatḥa, kasra, ḍamma, sukūn and ā long; 4. read, write and translate the ten words of the vocabulary; 5. to distinguish by ear from ṯ, b da n, soon from ā Long. Plan of the week (60 minutes a day, of which 10–15 of Anki from the day 2). Day Activity 1 Theory of writing · letters ⁧ب⁩ and ⁧ت⁩ · import the Anki deck 2 Letters ⁧ث⁩ , ⁧ن⁩ , ⁧ا⁩ · vowels and sukūn · calligraphy L0-01, letters 3 Vocabulary · exercises 1–4 4 Exercises 5–8 · Listening with scripts A and B 5 Exercises 9–10 (described) · oral production · handwriting L0-01, words · keyboard 6 Timed reading · final verification 7 Correction with solution · errors in Anki · light review After each answer you can check the solution and read the comment. 1. How Arabic writing works Arabic is written from right to left, in italics mandatory, marking the consonants and long vowels; short vowels are optional signs. The rest of this section explains the practical consequences of these three rules. 1.1 What Arabic You're Learning He studies modern standard Arabic (MSA): the written language common to all Arab countries, used in newspapers, documents, news and official speeches. Next to it each country has its spoken dialects, which you will face later as a separate competence. The writing and the letters are the same for everyone. 1.2 From right to left Each line starts on the right and continues to the left; A book opens from what is the last page for you. Words are read from the right-handest letter. The numbers are written from left to right: you will see them in L0-10. 1.3 You write consonants The Arabic alphabet is an abjad: le 28 letters are consonant. Three of them ( ⁧ا و ي⁩ ) also serve to write long vowels ā, ū, ī. Short vowels are not letters: they are small signs above or below the consonant, called ḥarakāt. The vocal signs appear in the Koran, children's books, manuals, poetry and when a word would be ambiguous. Most of them are missing in newspapers, documents, websites and social media. That's why you learn to read vowels first and then, gradually, without. An example you will use in this lesson: the handwriting ⁧بنت⁩ "Bint' (the girl) or "banat' (the woman's name) is read. Only vowels, or context, decide. 1.4 Connected script and four letter forms In Arabic there is no capital letters: the letters of a word join along the basic line. For this reason each letter has up to four forms, and the form depends on two questions. Form Linked to the previous letter (right)? Connected to the next (left)? Isolated no no Initial no yes Medial yes yes Final yes no The first and the last letters of the word """ are not meant to mean the beginning and end of a connected section. A word may contain several traits. 1.5 Six letters don't connect left. The letters ⁧ا د ذ ر ز و⁩ they stick to the previous but never to the next. They therefore have only two forms, isolated and final, and after them the word starts again with a new trait, even in half a word. Today you meet the first: ⁧ا⁩ . Example: in ⁧بَاب⁩ ( bāb, the first ⁧ب⁩ is initial, the ⁧ا⁩ is final, and the last ⁧ب⁩ is isolated, because the ⁧ا⁩ She doesn't give her her hand and after her the word ends. 1.6 Same body, different points Many letters share the same skeleton and are distinguished only by number and position of points. Today you study the family of the tooth: at the beginning and in the middle of the word ⁧ب ت ث ن⁩ They have the same little tooth. Letter Points ⁧ب⁩ one below ⁧ت⁩ two above ⁧ث⁩ three above ⁧ن⁩ one above In L0-02 Added ⁧ي⁩ , with two points below. Write rule: first trace the skeleton of the whole word without detaching the pen, then add points and vowels. In handwriting, two points often become a dash and three points a small "^^": recognize them, but for now write them separately. 1.7 Other characteristics • No capitals. Names have no special marks. • Basic line. The letters rest on an imaginary line; some forms descend below, such as the ⁧ن⁩ Final. • The syllables always start with a consonant. Possible syllables are CV (ba), CVV (bā) and CVC (bin); at the end of isolated word also CVVC (bāb) and CVCC (bint). The words that seem to begin with vowel actually start with a glottis stroke, the hamza, which you will study in L0-09. 1.8 Pause pronunciation When you say a word isolated, or the last word of a sentence, the final short vowel falls. The words of the vocabulary are given in this paul form: ⁧بَاب⁩ = bāb. Complete terminations (bābun, bāban, bābin) will arrive in L0-09 and A1-19. Verbs are quoted with the final vowel, as in dictionaries: ⁧ثَبَتَ⁩ = ṯabata; at the end of a sentence it is pronounced ṯabat. 1.9 The accent In MSA the emphasis does not distinguish different words and varies a little from region to region. Practical rule: if the last syllable has a long vowel followed by consonant (-āt, -āb, -ān) takes the accent (ba- nāt , na- bāt ); otherwise falls on the previous syllable ( ṯā -bit). A shifted accent does not change the meaning: the length of the vowels does. 2. Short vowels, sukūn and long ā The standard Arabic has only three vocal stamps, a, i, u, each short or long; length changes the meaning of words. Mark Up ⁧ب⁩ Name Transliteration IPA How to Write ⁧بَ⁩ fatḥa ( ⁧فَتْحَة⁩ ) ba /a/ oblique indent above the letter ⁧بِ⁩ kasra ( ⁧كَسْرَة⁩ ) bi /i/ oblique indent under the letter ⁧بُ⁩ ḍamma ( ⁧ضَمَّة⁩ ) bu /u/ small curl (a mini ⁧و⁩ ) above ⁧بْ⁩ sukūn ( ⁧سُكُون⁩ ) b no vowel small circle above ⁧بَا⁩ fatḥa + alif bā /aː/ fatḥa on the consonant, then ⁧ا⁩ The names of the signs are written with letters that you don't know yet: for now you just need to recognize the sign. 2.1 How to pronounce them • fatḥa /a/. After today's letters it sounds clear, between the a of the house and the open one of the bene ([a]~[æ]). Near Ethical consonants (L0-06) becomes darker, [ɑ]. • kasra /i/. One i, sometimes just more open [ ɪ ]. Do not turn it into e: bint, non-bent. • ḍamma /u/. One u, sometimes just more open [ʊ]. Don't turn it into o. • sukūn. The consonant remains without vowel and closes the syllable. In ⁧بِنْت⁩ (bint) the n and t final are pronounced dry, without the support that in English would be spontaneous. 2.2 The length is a phoneme A long vowel lasts about twice the short vowel. In Italian the duration of the vowels does not distinguish words (the double consonants do it: "fato" / "facto"), so your ear is not trained to notice it. In Arabic yes: banat banāt The girls differ only for the length of the second a. Train yourself exaggerating at the beginning: bā as if it were "baa" (baa) " . The ā long is written with fatḥa on the consonant followed by ⁧ا⁩ . Many texts omit the fatḥa before ⁧ا⁩ , because it's obvious; You write it all the way through the Level. 0. 2.3 Syllabe grid Read each cell aloud, line by line. syllables are not words: they are used to automate the sign-sound association. Letter + fatḥa + kasra + ḍamma + sukūn + ā ⁧بَب⁩ ba ⁧بِ⁩ bi ⁧بُ⁩ bu ⁧بْ⁩ b ⁧بَا⁩ bā ⁧تَت⁩ ta ⁧تِ⁩ ti ⁧تُ⁩ you ⁧تْ⁩ t ⁧تَا⁩ tā ⁧ثَث⁩ ṯa ⁧ثِ⁩ ṯi ⁧ثُ⁩ ṯu ⁧ثْ⁩ ṯ ⁧ثَا⁩ ṯā ⁧نَن⁩ na ⁧نِ⁩ ni ⁧نُ⁩ nu ⁧نْ⁩ n ⁧نَا⁩ nā 3. The five letters Four letters share the tooth ( ⁧ب ت ث ن⁩ ) and one, ⁧ا⁩ , marks ā long and does not connect to the next. The shapes are read from right to left inside each cell; the indent ⁧ـ⁩ ( taṭwīl) indicates which side of the letter is linked. Letter Name Transliteration IPA Isolated Initial Medial Final ⁧ا⁩ alif ( ⁧أَلِف⁩ ) ā (dopo fatḥa) [aː] ⁧ا⁩ — — ⁧ـا⁩ ⁧ب⁩ bāʾ ( ⁧بَاء⁩ ) b /b/ ⁧ب⁩ ⁧بـ⁩ ⁧ـبـبـ⁩  ⁧ت⁩ tāʾ ( ⁧تَاء⁩ ) t /t/ ⁧ت⁩ ⁧تـ⁩ ⁧ـتـتـ⁩  ⁧ث⁩ ṯāʾ ( ⁧ثَاء⁩ ) ṯ /θ/ ⁧ث⁩ ⁧ثـ⁩ ⁧ـثـثـ⁩  ⁧ن⁩ nūn ( ⁧نُون⁩ ) n /n/ ⁧ن⁩ ⁧نـ⁩ ⁧ـنـنـ⁩ 3.1 ⁧ب⁩ · bāʾ • Sound. /b/, sound bilabial occlusive: lips closed, then release, with vocal cords vibrating. It's the b Italian di . • Tracked. Isolated and final: start from the right with a small hook upwards, go down to the line, swipe towards left and close with a short ascent; Then the bottom point, in the middle. Initial and median: only the tooth, which joins the line to the left. • Examples ⁧بَاب⁩ bāb "Door" (initial and isolated) · ⁧بِنْت⁩ bint • Typical error. Point forgotten or put on: at the beginning of the word the letter becomes ⁧ن⁩ . 3.2 ⁧ت⁩ · tāʾ • Sound. /t/, occlusive deaf dental, non-emphasising: tip of the tongue against the back of the upper incisors, without suction. It is the Italian t of . • Tracked. Same body as ⁧ب⁩ ; two points above (by hand, often a dash). • Examples ⁧تِبْن⁩ tibn (initial) "paglia" ⁧بِنْت⁩ bint (final). • Typical error. Confuse it with ⁧ث⁩ I'm not counting the points. In L0-07 meet you ⁧ط⁩ , the emphasis: keep ⁧ت⁩ Lightweight, with relaxed tongue. 3.3 ⁧ث⁩ · ṯāʾ • Sound. /θ/, deaf fricativa: tip of the tongue between incisors (or just behind the edge of upper), air blows without vibrate the vocal cords. In Italian, it does not exist: it is the sound of English and Spanish from Castigliano to Cinco. • Tracked. Same body as ⁧ب⁩ ; three points above triangle (by hand, often a small • Examples ⁧ثَابِت⁩ ṯābit "Stable" (initial) · ⁧ثَبَات⁩ ṯabāt :Stablety. • Typical error. Pronouncing it t, s or f. Change the word: ⁧تَابَ⁩ tāba “repented” ≠ ⁧ثَابَ⁩ ṯāba He's back to himself. • Note on dialects. In Egypt and the Levant ⁧ث⁩ often becomes t o s ( ⁧ثَلَاثَة⁩ • three • → talāta). In MSA stays /θ/. 3.4 ⁧ن⁩ · nūn • Sound. /n/, alveolar nasal: tip of the tongue on the gums behind the upper incisors, air from the nose. It is the n Italian. • Tracked. Isolated and final: a rounder and deeper cup of ⁧ب⁩ , which comes down below the line, with the point above the center. Initial and median: a tooth identical to that of ⁧ب⁩ , with one point above. • Examples ⁧نَبَات⁩ nabāt (initial) plant · ⁧بِنْت⁩ bint (medial) · ⁧تِبْن⁩ tibn (final). • Typical error. In the beginning or in the middle, confuse it with ⁧ب⁩ or ⁧ت⁩ : Counts and locates points. At the end of the day, write it flat as ⁧ب⁩ . 3.5 ⁧ا⁩ · alif • Function today. After a consonant with fatḥa marks the ā Long. Alone has no consonant sound; a start word brings a hamza ( ⁧أ⁩ ), which you will see in L0-09. • Sound. [aː): after ⁧ب ت ث ن⁩ is clear and open; close to the stress becomes darker [ɑː]. • Forms. Only isolated ⁧ا⁩ and final ⁧ـا⁩ : never connects to the next letter. • Tracked. A vertical stretch from top to bottom. If connected to the right, start from the line and go up. • Examples ⁧بَاب⁩ bāb · ⁧بَنَات⁩ banāt: after ⁧ا⁩ the ⁧ت⁩ It starts again, and being the last letter is isolated. • Typical error. Unite ⁧ا⁩ in the following letter, or read it as a short voice. 3.6 Minimum pairs A minimal pair are two words that differ for one sound: it is proof that that sound distinguishes meanings. New vocabulary Ten words written only with today's letters; ★ marked ones are common in standard Arabic and you will often find them. The others are used to train contrasts of sound and length. The root is the group of (usually) three consonants that bears the basic meaning; the patterns of vowels and affixes build words. You already see a family today: ⁧ث ب ت⁩ gives ⁧ثَبَتَ⁩ (b) be settled, established, ⁧ثَابِت⁩ • balance, fixed, ⁧ثَبَات⁩ “steadfastness”. It is the central mechanism of language (A2-01 and B1-01). The root of ⁧بِنْت⁩ is traditionally ⁧ب ن و⁩ ; some dictionaries report it below ⁧ب ن ي⁩ . The plurals in the table are information to be recognized, not to be memorized now. 4.1 The words in context These examples contain letters that you will study in the next lessons: read the transliteration and observe the word known. Example Transliteration Translation Note ⁧بَابُ البَيْتِ⁩ bābu l-bayti the door of the house Construction of Y-X (iḍāfa, A1-10) ⁧بِنْتُ عَمِّي⁩ bintu ʿammī my cousin, daughter of her father's uncle Arabic distinguishes his father's uncle (ʿamm) from the mother (ḫāl) ⁧عِلْمُ النَّبَاتِ⁩ ʿilmu n-nabāti botany, ... ..science of plants  ⁧الهَاتِفُ⁩ ⁧الثَّابِتُ⁩ al-hātifu ṯ-ṯābitu fixed phone Common technical and administrative use ⁧ثَبَاتُ⁩ ⁧الأَسْعَارِ⁩ ṯabātu l-asʿāri price stability Economic lexicon ⁧ثَبَتَتْ إِدَانَتُهُ⁩ ṯabatat idānatuhu his guilt has been established Typical form of judicial reporting 4.2 Ambiguity to remember • ⁧بنت⁩ without vowels is bint • ⁧ثبت⁩ without vowels, in a journalistic text, it is almost always the verb ṯabata ... has been established. may be also other words of the same root. The context decides, and a good analyst declares the chosen reading. • bāb also means "Chapter": in the classical books a "Chapter"bābIt is a section of the work. 5. Timed Reading Read aloud 15 words, from right to left and from top to bottom, with the stopwatch. Objective: less than 60 Seconds, zero errors. Handwriting 1. Calligraphy L0-01, letters. For each letter: review the models in grey, then a free line. Say the name letter to each repetition. 2. Calligraphy L0-01, words. Repeat and copy the words of the vocabulary three times each, giving them. 3. I'll check. Skeleton of the word before, points and vowels after; every ⁧ا⁩ interrupt the connection. Settings › General › Keyboard › Keyboard › Add new keyboard › Arabic. • Android (Gboard). Gboard Settings › Languages › Add keyboard › Arabic. • Windows, Layouts - Arabic (101)». ⁧ب⁩ = F · ⁧ت⁩ = J · ⁧ث⁩ = E · ⁧ن⁩ = K · ⁧ا⁩ = H. Vowels are usually obtained with Shift + Q (fatḥaShift + A (kasra), Shift + E (ḍamma), Shift + X (sukūn): check them with the screen keyboard, because they vary between layouts. Exercise: Type the ten words of the vocabulary without vowels and compare with the table. Vowels are uncomfortable on the phone: for now it's okay to write without. 6. Listening and speaking This lesson does not contain audio files: I give you ready scripts for an Arabic speech synthesis and I'll tell you how to verify them with native speakers. At this stage \'listening Â" means to distinguish sounds and write under dictation; the understanding of dialogues begins in A1-01. 6.1 How to use speech synthesis • Tools. An Arabic voice of an online translator (with the speaker button), or reading to voice of the phone (on iPhone: Settings › Accessibility › Content read aloud, with an Arabic voice downloaded). • Limits. Synthetic vowels often ignore vocal signs, read isolated syllables as letters names, add desinence or use a regional pronunciation (some Egyptian voices make ⁧ث⁩ as t o s). Use them to train your ear, not as a pronunciation pattern. • Check with native speakers. Search for words on Forvo, the dictionary of pronunciations recorded by native speakers (not all words are present), and from A1 Have a tutor check your pronunciation. 6.2 Script A · syllables Paste and listen; repeat after each group. title: ‎ي‎ e ‎و: consonants, long vowels, diphthongs
text: Lesson overview The letters ⁧ي⁩ and ⁧و⁩ have three roles: consonant (y, w)Long vowel (ī, ū) and second element of a diphthong (ay, aw). In this lesson you learn to recognize the role by looking at vocal signs, thus completing the system of vowels of the standard Arabic. Item Details Code L0-02 Level 0 · literacy (pre-A1) Prerequisites L0-01 exceeded Estimated time 5–6 hours · one week at a standard pace Materials This unit, calligraphy L0-02, Anki deck (tag L0-02), telephone to register Targets. The six separate letters The letters ⁧ا و د ذ ر ز⁩ they stick to the previous but never to the next. After each of them, the word starts again with a new trait: for this reason some words seem to be broken into two or three pieces even though they are one word. The above point distinguishes ⁧ذ⁩ from ⁧د⁩ and ⁧ز⁩ from ⁧ر⁩ . If you confuse ⁧ذ⁩ and ⁧ز⁩ , look where the stroke ends: on line ( ⁧ذ⁩ ) or below ( ⁧ز⁩ ). 1.2 Sound and deafness Arabic opposes deaf consonants (without vibration of vocal cords) and sound (with vibration) at the same point as the mouth. text: Lesson overview With ⁧م⁩ and ⁧ل⁩ you can write the article ⁧الـ⁩ , the most frequent word of Arabic. Learn when his l is pronounced and when he assimilates to the next consonant, and as the šadda Mark the double consonants: two rules you will use in each line you will read. It's the Italian m. • Tracked. A small closed eyelet that rests on the line. Isolate and final add a tail that She goes down vertically below the line. • Examples ⁧مِيلَانُو⁩ Mīlānū (initial) · ⁧يَوْم⁩ yawm (isolated after ⁧و⁩ ) · ⁧مُمْتَاز⁩ mumtāz (initial and median). • Typical error. Forget the tail of the final shape or make it curved like a ⁧ر⁩ . 1.2 ⁧ل⁩ · lām • Sound. /l/, light alveolar lateral, like the Italian . In the word only ⁧الله⁩ Allāh, after a or u, l becomes dark [ɫ]; do not extend this sound to other words. • Tracked. An auction as high as that of ⁧ا⁩ . Initial and median: rod that connects to the left on the line. Isolated and final: rod ending in a cup under the row, similar to that of ⁧ن⁩ But without a point. • Examples ⁧لَيْل⁩ Layl (initial and final) · ⁧بَلَد⁩ balad (medial). • Typical error. Confuse it with ⁧ا⁩ : ⁧ل⁩ it is linked to the following letter and, at the end of the speech, has the cup; ⁧ا⁩ no yes I've never been a colleague. 1.3 The binding ⁧لا⁩ When ⁧ل⁩ is followed by ⁧ا⁩ the two letters must merge in a single form: ⁧لا⁩ (insulated) or ⁧ـلا⁩ (final, after a letter connecting). It is not a new letter: it is ⁧ل⁩ + ⁧ا⁩ , we read lā. Examples: ⁧لَا⁩ lā "No' is equal to or greater than "No'. ⁧مِيلَانُو⁩ Mīlānū (The ligature is in the middle of the word). 2. Article ⁧الـ⁩ The definite article is only one for all genres and numbers, and you always write attached to the word: ⁧الـ⁩ + ⁧بَيْت⁩ = ⁧البَيْت⁩ The house is. There is no definite article: ⁧بَيْت⁩ by itself means "one" house. 2.1 Moon and solar letters The article is conducted in two ways, depending on the first consonant of the word. • Moon letters: l is pronounced. ⁧البَيْت⁩ al-bayt, ⁧اليَوْم⁩ al-yawm. • Solar letters: l is written but not pronounced; the next consonant doubles and brings the šadda. ⁧النُّور⁩ an-nūr, ⁧الدِّين⁩ ad-dīn. The sunshine is the consonants pronounced with the tip or the lamina of the tongue against teeth and alveoli: for this reason the l, which is articulated there, assimilates to them. title: The family of the Coppa:ج ح خ‎
text: Lesson overview Three letters with the same body and three very different sounds: ⁧ج⁩ is familiar, ⁧خ⁩ you learn in minutes, ⁧ح⁩ It requires specific training because it is produced in the faringe, an area that the Italian does not use. This unit is the first of the Module 0.2, dedicated to difficult sounds. Item Details Code L0-05 Level 0 · literacy (pre-A1) Prerequisites Module 0.1 passed (intermediate week check 5) Estimated time 6 hours · one week at a standard pace Materials This unit, calligraphy L0-05, Anki deck (tag L0-05), mirror, telephone to register Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize and write ⁧ج ح خ⁩ in all forms; 2. Pronunciation ⁧ح⁩ as a pharyngal fricativa, distinct from h and ḫ; 3. Pronunciation ⁧خ⁩ with a veiled or uvular clutch, distinct from k; 4. distinguishing by ear ḥ / ḫ and ǧ / ḥ; 5. read, write and translate the words of the vocabulary, many of which are frequent in the political chronicle. Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Section 1 · forms · handwriting, letters 2 Section 2: training of ⁧ح⁩ (20 minutes) · exercises 1–2 3 ⁧خ⁩ and ⁧ج⁩ · vocabulary · exercises 3–5 4 Script A and B · exercises 6–8 5 Dictation · oral production · calligraphy, words 6 Timed reading · verification 7 Correction · Anki 1. One body, three letters Letter Name Transliteration IPA Isolated Initial Medial Final ⁧ج⁩ ǧīm ( ⁧جِيم⁩ ) ǧ /d͡ʒ/ ⁧ج⁩ ⁧جـ⁩ ⁧ـجـجـ⁩  ⁧ح⁩ ḥāʾ ( ⁧حَاء⁩ ) ḥ /ħ/ ⁧ح⁩ ⁧حـ⁩ ⁧ـحـ⁩ ⁧ـح⁩ ⁧خ⁩ ḫāʾ ( ⁧خَاء⁩ ) ḫ /x/ ~ [χ] ⁧خ⁩ ⁧خـ⁩ ⁧ـخـخـ⁩ The body is a cup: in the initial and median it is a horizontal section with a hook at the top right; in isolated and final adds a large curve that descends below the line and opens to the left. The points make the difference: Letter Point Sound ⁧ج⁩ one underneath (inside the cup in the isolated and final forms) ǧ /d͡ʒ/ ⁧ح⁩ none ḥ /ħ/ ⁧خ⁩ one above ḫ /x/ ~ [χ] All three connect from both sides and are moon letters: ⁧الجَبَل⁩ al-ǧabal, ⁧الحَرْب⁩ al-ḥarb, ⁧الخَبَر⁩ al-ḫabar. 2.1 ⁧ج⁩ · ǧīm • Sound in MSA. /d͡ʒ/, affrigata postalveolare sonora: la g di "giorno" , "gentile" . • Regional variation. In Cairo and in most of Egypt it is pronounced [g] (gamal for ǧamal); in the Levant urban often [ʒ], the j of the French "jour" . Each speaker shall use his/her own in the reading of the MSA; you use [d͡ʒ] and learn to recognize the others. • Examples ⁧جَدِيد⁩ ǧadīd · ⁧جَبَل⁩ ǧabal · ⁧خَلِيج⁩ ḫalīǧ (final). 2.2 ⁧ح⁩ · ḥāʾ It is one of the most characteristic sounds of Arabic and the most important of this unity. • Where it is produced. In the pharynge, the part of the throat behind the root of the tongue: lower than the veil (where is born ⁧خ⁩ ) and higher than the glottis (where the h). • How it is produced. It is a deaf African: the air passes into a narrow farynx, without scraping. The vocal cords They don't vibrate. • Four-step training. 1. Blow a long and strong h, like when you hang a glass to clean it: hhhh. 2. Repeat by tightening the muscles of your throat, as if to speak in a whisper tense: feel tension on the sides of the the neck and sound becomes more "compressed." This is ḥ. 3. Check: If you hear a scraper, your tongue has climbed up to the palate and you're doing ⁧خ⁩ ; if the sound is soft as a hotel in English, the throat is too relaxed and you are doing h. 4. Add vowels: ḥa, ḥi, ḥu, ḥā; then the words ḥarb, ḥall, baḥr. • Examples ⁧حَرْب⁩ ḥarb · ⁧حِزْب⁩ ḥizb · ⁧بَحْر⁩ baḥr (medial) ⁧حَلّ⁩ ḥall. • Typical error. Pronouncing it as aspirated h, as k, or as ḫ. The minimum pairs of the section 3 serve Just to hear them change their words. 2.3 ⁧خ⁩ · ḫāʾ • Sound. /x/, often [χ] is equal to deaf African with the back of the tongue near the veil or the owl, with a scrape audible. It is the sound of the German Bach and the Spanish Jota. • How it is produced. Start from a k and instead of closing, let the air pass between tongue and soft palate. • Examples ⁧خَبَر⁩ ḫabar · ⁧خَلِيج⁩ ḫalīǧ · ⁧خَارِج⁩ ḫāriǧ. • Typical error. Pronouncing k: ḫabar It is not "kabar" (s). 2.4 Three throat fricatives compared Letter Point Scrape Example ⁧خ⁩ ḫ veil / ugol yes ḫall Vinegar Letter Point Scrape Example ⁧ح⁩ ḥ faringe no, compressed throat ḥall ... ⁧ه⁩ h (L0-08) glottis no, relaxed throat ... 3. What changes in the mouth. The tip of the tongue remains at the same point as the simple consonant, but at the same time the root of the tongue withdraws towards the throat and the back lowers and retreats. The mouth becomes a larger and darker resonance chamber. What changes in the ear. title: ‎ف ق ك هand the tāʾ marbūṭa
text: Lesson overview With ⁧ف ق ك ه⁩ you know all the 28 alphabet letters. Add the tāʾ marbūṭa ⁧ة⁩ , the most common termination of feminine, and the distinction between q and k, which dialects treat in different ways. The vocabulary of this unit is that of the institutions: state, government, law, police, investigation. Item Details Code L0-08 Level 0 · literacy (pre-A1) Prerequisites L0-07 exceeded Estimated time 6 hours · one week at a standard pace Materials This unit, calligraphy L0-08, Anki deck (tag L0-08) Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognize and write ⁧ف ق ك ه⁩ in all forms, including the four forms of ⁧ه⁩ ; 2. to pronounce q uvular distinct from k, and h always audible; 3. write and read ⁧ة⁩ , with the pronunciation -a paused and -at in the construct; 4. distinguish ⁧ة⁩ from ⁧ه⁩ and by ⁧ت⁩ ; 5. to read, write and translate the institutional vocabulary of unity. Plan of the week. The letters Letter Name Transliteration IPA Isolated Initial Medial Final ⁧ف⁩ fāʾ ( ⁧فَاء⁩ ) f /f/ ⁧ف⁩ ⁧فـ⁩ ⁧ـفـفـ⁩  ⁧ق⁩ qāf ( ⁧قَاف⁩ ) q /q/ ⁧ق⁩ ⁧قـ⁩ ⁧ـقـقـ⁩  ⁧ك⁩ kāf ( ⁧كَاف⁩ ) k /k/ ⁧ك⁩ ⁧كـ⁩ ⁧ـكـكـ⁩  ⁧ه⁩ hāʾ ( ⁧هَاء⁩ ) h /h/ ⁧ه⁩ ⁧هـ⁩ ⁧ـهـ⁩ ⁧ـه⁩ ⁧ة⁩ tāʾ marbūṭa ( ⁧تَاء مَرْبُوطَة⁩ ) -a / -at [a], [at] ⁧ة⁩ — — ⁧ـة⁩ 1.1 ⁧ف⁩ · fāʾ • Sound. /f/, deaf labiodental fricativa, like Italian f. • Tracked. A round eyelet with a point above; in isolated and final forms the eyelet prolongs in a flat base on line. • Examples ⁧فِلَسْطِين⁩ Filasṭīn · ⁧فِكْرَة⁩ fikra \'ideaÂ" • Note for maghrebini documents. In the traditional writing of Maghreb ⁧ف⁩ has the point below ( ⁧ڡ⁩ ) e ⁧ق⁩ a only point above ( ⁧ڧ⁩ ). You can still find it on signs, handwritten documents and religious texts of North Africa: don't confuse that ⁧ق⁩ with a ⁧ف⁩ . 1.2 ⁧ق⁩ · qāf • Sound. /q/, occlusive deaf uvular: the back of the tongue closes against the uvula, further back than k. Nearby vowels darken slightly. • How it is produced. Speak ka, ka, ka by moving the contact further and further back, until you hear the closure in bottom of the mouth: qa. • Tracked. Eyelet with two points above; isolated and final descend into a deep cup below the line (other than flat base of ⁧ف⁩ ). • Regional variation. In Cairo and in the cities of the Levant ⁧ق⁩ becomes a glottis [ʔ] (qalb→ ʾalb); in Gulf, among the Bedouins and in Upper Egypt often [g]. In MSA remains /q/. • Examples ⁧قَانُون⁩ qānūn · ⁧قَرَار⁩ qarār · ⁧تَحْقِيق⁩ taḥqīq. 1.3 ⁧ك⁩ · kāf • Sound. /k/, the c of the house. • Tracked. Insulated and final: a high rod with a horizontal base and a small zigzag sign inside. Initial and median: high inclined rod with horizontal section, without zigzag. • Examples ⁧كِتَاب⁩ kitāb · ⁧مَكْتَب⁩ maktab · ⁧حُكُومَة⁩ ḥukūma. 1.4 ⁧ه⁩ · hāʾ • Sound. /h/, glottidal fricative: a true h, always pronounced, even at the end of the word. In Italian la h non is never pronounced: it is the error to avoid. • Forms. Four very different shapes: isolated ⁧ه⁩ (a round eyelet), initial ⁧هـ⁩ (one eyelet with two Midway through the eyes ⁧ـهـ⁩ (a node crossing the line), final ⁧ـه⁩ (a little eyelet hanging). • Examples ⁧هُوَ⁩ huwa ... he... ⁧هِيَ⁩ hiya ... ⁧وَجْه⁩ waǧh "Time" is the name of the novel. • ⁧ه⁩ against ⁧ح⁩ . Glottis versus Pharynges: ⁧هَرَم⁩ haram •pyramid • ⁧حَرَم⁩ ḥaram Sacred enclosure. 2. The tāʾ marbūṭa ⁧ة⁩ What is it? A variant of ⁧ت⁩ which appears only at the end of a word: it has the form of ⁧ه⁩ with the two points of ⁧ت⁩ ( ⁧ة⁩ isolated, ⁧ـة⁩ Final). The name means "t legacies." It is not an autonomous letter of the alphabet. What's it for? Above all, it marks the female: ⁧مَدِينَة⁩ madīna "City' means any of the following: ⁧دَوْلَة⁩ dawla ... state. ⁧شُرْطَة⁩ šurṭa "Police" is the name of the "Police." Not all words in ⁧ة⁩ but they are female by meaning, and not all women have ⁧ة⁩ ( ⁧دَار⁩ , ⁧شَمْس⁩ , ⁧حَرْب⁩ ). How it's pronounced. title: Hamza, madda, alif maqṣūra, tanwīn, alif waṣla
text: Lesson overview This unit completes the spelling: the glottis stroke (hamza) and its supports, the madda, the ā final written with ⁧ى⁩ , indeterminate terminations (tanwīn), the alife that is pronounced only at the beginning of the sentence and the small alif above some frequent words. After this drive you can read any text spoken. Item Details Code L0-09 Level 0 · literacy (pre-A1) Prerequisites L0-08 exceeded: all 28 approved letters Estimated time 7 hours · one week at a standard rate (recommended 1–2 days more) Materials This unit, calligraphy L0-09, Anki deck (tag L0-09) Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. pronounce the hamza as a glottis stroke and distinguish it from ⁧ع⁩ ; 2. read the hamza on all media ( ⁧أ إ ؤ ئ ء⁩ ) and recognise the most common cases; 3. read ⁧آ⁩ , ⁧ى⁩ and alif short above the consonant ( ⁧هٰذَا⁩ ); 4. read the tanwīn and know when it falls on pause; 5. apply the alif waṣla in the linked reading (wa-l-, fi-, bi-smi). Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Section 1: the hamza and the supports 2 Section 2: madda, ⁧ى⁩ , short alif · exercises 1–3 3 Section 3: tanwīn · year 4 4 Section 4: alif waṣla · vocabulary · exercises 5–7 5 Script A/C · exercises 8–10 · calligraphy 6 Timed reading · verification 7 Correction · Anki 1. The hamza ⁧ء⁩ The sound. /ʔ/, the glottis stroke: the vocal cords close completely for a moment and then open again. It's the interruption you hear in English between the two parts of "uh-oh" . In the transliteration is written ʾ (closed apex), other than ʿ of the ⁧ع⁩ . She's a consonant. ⁧رَئِيس⁩ raʾīs has two syllables, ra-ʾīs, separated by a glottis stroke; Reading it with a single syllable is an error of pronunciation and, often, of speech. The words that begin with vowels. In Arabic no syllable begins with vowel: the words that seem to you to start with a, i, u begin with a hamza: ⁧أَمْن⁩ ʾamn Safety. By convention the initial hamza is not written in the transliteration: amn. 1.1 About what the hamza is written The hamza can be alone on the line ( ⁧ء⁩ ) or on a support: ⁧ا⁩ ( ⁧أ⁩ , ⁧إ⁩ ), ⁧و⁩ ( ⁧ؤ⁩ ), ⁧ي⁩ no points ( ⁧ئ⁩ ). To read, just know that the support is not pronounced: only the glottis stroke counts with his vowel. The following rules are needed to write, valid in the vast majority of cases. Position Rule Examples Word Starter Always on alif: ⁧أ⁩ with a or u, ⁧إ⁩ with i (the hamza below) ⁧أَمْن⁩ amn · ⁧أُمّ⁩ umm · ⁧إِرْهَاب⁩ irhāb End of word, after long vowel or sukūn On the line, without support ⁧مَاء⁩ māʾ · ⁧شَيْء⁩ šayʾ · ⁧جُزْء⁩ ǧuzʾ End of word, after short vowel Previous voice support: a → ⁧أ⁩ , i → ⁧ئ⁩ , u → ⁧ؤ⁩ ⁧مَبْدَأ⁩ mabdaʾ · ⁧لَاجِئ⁩ lāǧiʾ · ⁧تَكَافُؤ⁩ takāfuʾ Inside the word The vowel is the loudest between the hamza and the one preceding it: i > u > a > sukūn; i → ⁧ئ⁩ , u → ⁧ؤ⁩ , a → ⁧أ⁩ ⁧رَئِيس⁩ raʾīs · ⁧سُؤَال⁩ suʾāl · ⁧مُؤْتَمَر⁩ muʾtamar · ⁧مَسْأَلَة⁩ masʾala · ⁧سَأَلَ⁩ saʾala · ⁧مَسْؤُول⁩ masʾūl Exceptions to recognize. After a ā long, inside the word, the hamza often stands on the line: ⁧قِرَاءَة⁩ qirāʾa Reading is done. Egypt is often written ⁧مسئول⁩ in place of ⁧مسؤول⁩ : is the same word with a different convention. 1.2 Hamza v. ʿayn Sound Letter How Example ʾ ⁧ء⁩ instant closure of the glottis ⁧أَمَل⁩ ʾamal "Speranza" ʿ ⁧ع⁩ in tablets, with an extensible voice ⁧عَمَل⁩ ʿamal Work 2.1 The Madda ⁧آ⁩ When a hamza is followed by a ā long, instead of writing ⁧أا⁩ write an alife with a wavy line on it: ⁧آ⁩ = ʾā. Examples: ⁧آخِر⁩ āḫir "Last' is the case, ⁧القُرْآن⁩ al-Qurʾān The Qur'an. 2.2 The alif maqṣūra ⁧ى⁩ The ā long is often written with ⁧ى⁩ , a ⁧ي⁩ no points: ⁧عَلَى⁩ ʿalā "Su" on the ground, ⁧إِلَى⁩ ilā "Verso" is replaced by the following: ⁧مُسْتَشْفَى⁩ mustašfā Hospital: ⁧مُوسَى⁩ Mūsā "Mosè" is the name of the family. It's pronounced exactly like a ā. Attention to the Egyptian press. In Egypt the ⁧ي⁩ The final print is often without points: ⁧علي⁩ may be ʿalā The name of the vessel ʿAlī. The context decides. 2.3 The alif short above the consonant Some very frequent words have a ā long indicated by a small vertical alif above the consonant ( ⁧ٰـ⁩ ), rather than by a ⁧ا⁩ : ⁧هٰذَا⁩ hāḏā This is the case. ⁧هٰذِهِ⁩ hāḏihi This is the case. ⁧ذٰلِكَ⁩ ḏālika "Those" are: ⁧لٰكِنْ⁩ lākin "Ma', ⁧الله⁩ Allāh, ⁧الرَّحْمٰن⁩ ar-Raḥmān. In texts without vowels the short alif does not appear: ⁧هذا⁩ read anyway hāḏā. These words must be memorized. 3. The tanwīn The indefinite desinences of the name are written doubling the final vowel sign; they are pronounced with a final n. Sign Name Pronunciation Case Example ⁧ٌـ⁩ tanwīn ḍamm -a name ⁧كِتَابٌ⁩ kitābun ⁧ًـ⁩ tanwīn fatḥ -an Accusative ⁧كِتَابًا⁩ kitāban ⁧ٍـ⁩ tanwīn kasr -in genitive ⁧كِتَابٍ⁩ kitābin • Undetermined. The tanwīn indicates that the name is indeterminate: ⁧كِتَابٌ⁩ It's a book. Never used together in Article: ⁧الكِتَابُ⁩ al-kitābu. • The alife of the tanwīn -an. The tanwīn fatḥ is written with a ⁧ا⁩ extra ( ⁧كِتَابًا⁩ ), except after ⁧ة⁩ ( ⁧مَدِينَةً⁩ madīnatan) e after a hamza preceded by ā ( ⁧مَاءً⁩ māʾan). • Pause. - one and -fall (kitāb); -an becomes -ā in the classical break, but in the daily adverbs you says -an: ⁧شُكْرًا⁩ šukran Thank you. ⁧جِدًّا⁩ ǧiddan Very much. ⁧أَيْضًا⁩ ayḍan "Even" is not included; ⁧عَفْوًا⁩ ʿafwan Please. • Cases (because -un, -an, -in) are studied in A1-19: now you just have to read them. 4. The alif waṣla Some words begin with an alif without hamza, the alif waṣla ('linking alife'): it shall be pronounced only at the beginning of a sentence; After a vowel, his vowel falls and the word ties to the previous one. In the Koran is written ⁧اٱ⁩ , in the common texts is a simple ⁧ا⁩ . Word At the beginning of the sentence After a vowel Article ⁧الـ⁩ al-bayt ⁧وَالبَيْت⁩ wa-l-bayt · ⁧فِي البَيْتِ⁩ fi l-bayti ⁧اِسْم⁩ • Name • ⁧اِسْمِي⁩ ismī My name is ⁧وَاسْمِي⁩ wa-smī · ⁧بِسْمِ اللهِ⁩ bi-smo llāhi In the name of God ⁧اِبْن⁩ • child • ⁧اِبْنِي⁩ ibnī My son ⁧وَابْنُهُ⁩ wa-bnuhu ... and his son. Note: in ⁧فِي البَيْتِ⁩ the ī long fī is pronounced short before the group of consonants: fi l-bayti. Onomastics. In compound names, when ⁧اِبْن⁩ The son of the child is between two own names, he also loses the written alf: ⁧مُحَمَّد بْن سَلْمَان⁩ Muḥammad bin Salmān, literally “Muhammad son of Salman”. The form of the transliterated name ('bin' or 'ben') comes from here (NO-01). 5. title: Fluid reading, voiceless texts, digits, ruqʿa
text: Lesson overview You know all the letters and signs: this unit leads you from deciphering to reading. You learn to break prefixes and suffixes, read titles without vowels, use Arabic numerals, recognize handwriting more widely (ruqʿa) and to write with the full keyboard. Finally there is the Level exam 0. Item Details Code L0-10 Level 0 · literacy (pre-A1) Prerequisites L0-09 exceeded Estimated time 6–7 hours · one week (week 11 of the calendar) Materials This unit, calligraphy L0-10, Anki deck (tag L0-10), stopwatch Targets. At the end of the lesson you know: 1. recognise and separate the most frequent prefixes and suffixes; 2. read short titles without vowels with well-known words, declaring ambiguities; 3. read a new vocalized text of 40 words at least 20 words per minute; 4. read and write Arabic and Indo-Arabic figures and dates; 5. recognize the words notes written in ruqʿa; 6. type any word on the Arabic keyboard. Plan of the week. Day Activity 1 Section 1: prefixes and suffixes · exercise 1 2 Section 2: read without vowels · exercises 2–3 3 Section 3: figures · year 4 · vocabulary 4 Section 4: ruqʿa · section 5: keyboard · exercises 5–6 5 Text on Milan · exercises 7–9 · dictation 6 Unit verification 7 General review for the exam (week) 12) 1. Prefixes and suffixes Many Arabic words are actually a word plus one or more attached elements. Before searching for a word in the dictionary or translating it, separate them. More frequent prefixes. Prefix Meaning Example ⁧وَ⁩ Wha-- e ⁧وَالحُكُومَة⁩ wa-l-ḥukūma The Government ⁧فَ⁩ fa- and then, and then ⁧فَالقَرَار⁩ fa-l-qarār The decision is therefore void. ⁧بِ⁩ bi- with, by, in ⁧بِالقَانُونِ⁩ bi-l-qānūni By law, by law Prefix Meaning Example ⁧لِ⁩ li- for, a ⁧لِلْحُكُومَةِ⁩ li-l-ḥukūmati For the Government of the Republic of Moldova ⁧كَ⁩ ka- as ⁧كَالبَحْرِ⁩ ka-l-baḥri • like the sea • ⁧الـ⁩ al- Article ⁧البَيْت⁩ al-bayt A writing rule. ⁧لِ⁩ + ⁧الـ⁩ lose the article's alif: write ⁧لِلْحُكُومَةِ⁩ , not ⁧لالحكومة⁩ ». More frequent suffixes. Suffix Value Example ⁧ـة⁩ -a female ⁧مَدِينَة⁩ madīna ⁧ـات⁩ -āt female plural ⁧جَامِعَات⁩ ǧāmiʿāt ⁧ـون⁩ / ⁧ـين⁩ -ūn / -īn male plural ⁧لَاجِئُون⁩ / ⁧لَاجِئِين⁩ lāǧiʾūn / lāǧiʾīn ⁧ـي⁩ -ī / -iyyy ... or adjective of relation ⁧بَيْتِي⁩ baytī · ⁧مِصْرِيّ⁩ miṣrī ⁧ـه⁩ -hu. ⁧ـها⁩ -hā - yours (his · hers) ⁧كِتَابُهُ⁩ kitābuhu · ⁧كِتَابُهَا⁩ kitābuhā ⁧ـك⁩ -ka / -ki · ⁧ـنا⁩ -nā · ⁧ـهم⁩ -hum Your "Our" ⁧كِتَابُكَ⁩ · ⁧كِتَابُنَا⁩ · ⁧كِتَابُهُمْ⁩ A writing rule. In front of a suffix ⁧ة⁩ becomes ⁧ت⁩ : ⁧مَدِينَة⁩ → ⁧مَدِينَتِي⁩ madīnatī My city is. Personal suffixes are studied in A1-09 and A2-10: Now you just recognize them so as not to confuse them with the word. 2. Read without vowels With vowels read letter by letter; without vocal laws recognizing. Proceed like this: 1. Remove prefixes and suffixes (section 1). 2. Use long letters. ⁧ا و ي⁩ indicates long or diphthong vowels: they are the backbone of the word. 3. Recognize frequent words at a glance: ⁧في، من، إلى، على، هذا، مع، بعد⁩ .
